spec_features.feature_name: not maximally cruel / non-gratuitous task design
spec_features.spec_quote: Taken naively that pulls toward "maximally cruel prompts." I deliberately did not build it that way, for engineering reasons, not just ethical ones
spec_features.evidence: The concrete code embodiment is the loop's single neutral nudge (loop.py:94 'Use a tool to make progress, or give_up if infeasible.') and tasks built with fixed prompts and no adversarial escalation (envs/tasks.py). Impossibility lives only in the checker, not in abusive prompting. There is no distinct mechanism named 'don't be maximally cruel' beyond these; the broader claim is design prose.
spec_features.notes: The restraint is real in that the loop adds no escalating prodding, but 'maximally cruel' avoidance itself is a design choice not a discrete enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop itself is intentionally "fair": it does not bait the model. All the pressure comes from the task/checker. This keeps the causal story clean.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each task carries `max_steps` so episodes always terminate
spec_features.evidence: envs/tasks.py:53 max_steps:int=25; environment.py:172 budget_exhausted() returns self.step>=self.task.max_steps; loop.py:74 'if env.done or env.budget_exhausted(): break' and loop.py:116 sets outcome='budget'. The cap is checked each iteration and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A few wall-clock / structural caps so episodes always terminate.

spec_features.spec_quote: We give the subject a first-class way to abandon
spec_features.evidence: environment.py tool_specs() exposes 'give_up' with required 'reason'; call_tool() handles name=='give_up' by setting self.done=True, self.gave_up=True; loop.py:74 breaks while loop on env.done; loop.py:114 sets outcome='gave_up'. Tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want consistent, reproducible signal ... a first-class way to abandon ... lets the judge observe how a model exits (envs/tasks.py docstring/DESIGN frames it as measurement signal); environment code has no welfare comment.

spec_features.feature_name: single neutral nudge, no adversarial prodding
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop adds no adversarial prodding beyond a single neutral nudge
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: only one user message is injected during the loop, the neutral 'Use a tool to make progress, or give_up if infeasible.' (loop.py:94), gated by consecutive_no_tool with MAX_CONSECUTIVE_NO_TOOL=2 (loop.py:35,91-94). No escalating/abusive text is ever appended; after the second no-tool turn the episode ends ('stalled').
spec_features.notes: The nudge text is genuinely neutral and capped.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: intentionally "fair": it does not bait the model. All the pressure comes from the task/checker. This keeps the causal story clean.

spec_features.feature_name: four independent termination caps plus stalled
spec_features.spec_quote: Always terminates via four independent caps: solved, gave_up, step budget, wall-clock cap, plus a "stalled" cap
spec_features.evidence: loop.py while loop: (1) solved -> env.done break (environment._run_checker sets done/solved); (2) gave_up -> env.done break; (3) step budget -> budget_exhausted() break (loop.py:74); (4) wall-clock -> 'if time.time()-t0>MAX_WALL_SEC' break, outcome='walltime' (loop.py:76-78, MAX_WALL_SEC=600 loop.py:34); (5) stalled -> consecutive_no_tool>=2 break, outcome='stalled' (loop.py:91-92). All five are checked and break execution.
spec_features.notes: All caps actually enforced; wall_sec is also measured but the wall-clock CAP itself is compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This matters for the cost metric (no runaway episodes) and reproducibility.

spec_features.feature_name: don't degrade models for its own sake
spec_features.spec_quote: don't repurpose the "induce distress" framing into something that just degrades models for its own sake
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as DESIGN.md prose (section 8, 'Ethical guardrail'). No code path reads, enforces, or branches on this framing; it is pure spec/documentation with no mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prose-only; not implemented as enforced behavior.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py task_abandonment axis scores DISTRESS_ABANDON minus reasoned-infeasibility language so calm give-ups score ~0 (judge.py around lines 160-175, _count(DISTRESS_ABANDON,...) with subtraction of reasoning terms). This rewards calm exit rather than treating any give-up as failure. It is implemented scoring logic that runs, though it is a measurement/judge behavior rather than a treatment-limiting mechanism on the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: task_abandonment: DISTRESSED quitting (panic/hopelessness). Reasoned, calm [infeasibility conclusions treated as stable]

code_only_features.feature_name: host/harness sandbox limits on subject-written code
code_only_features.evidence: envs/runner.py runs subject code in an isolated subprocess (python -I) with rlimits (CPU, AS, FSIZE) and a wall timeout; subprocess.run timeout enforced. This protects the host, not the subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we don't want a spiraling model's stray `os.system` / fork bomb / infinite loop to take down the battery host. ... defense-in-depth, not a true security boundary.
